## Lost events

| Events lost | trials | ACTIVE, right origin | ACTIVE, any origin | ACTIVE or WATCH | with gap-fill (ACTIVE, right origin) | stateless rules |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0% | 270 | 100.0 (99-100) | 100.0 (99-100) | 100.0 (99-100) | 100.0 (99-100) | 55.6 (50-61) |
| 5% | 270 | 93.3 (90-96) | 94.4 (91-97) | 94.1 (91-96) | 100.0 (99-100) | 51.9 (46-58) |
| 10% | 270 | 85.2 (80-89) | 87.8 (83-91) | 89.6 (85-93) | 100.0 (99-100) | 46.3 (40-52) |
| 20% | 270 | 76.3 (71-81) | 80.0 (75-84) | 83.3 (78-87) | 99.3 (97-100) | 43.3 (38-49) |
| 30% | 270 | 61.5 (56-67) | 68.5 (63-74) | 73.0 (67-78) | 99.3 (97-100) | 32.2 (27-38) |

'Any origin' counts an ACTIVE alert that blames the role session when the AssumeRole that issued its credential was lost: the privilege change is still caught, but the attacker is not named. Gap-fill assumes the event history returns the lost events (recall set by --gapfill-recall; validated on live AWS by experiments/live_gapfill.py).
